q: 'National Andhra Mahasabha' initiated/established
explanation:
Read as the 'Jatiya Andhra Mahasabha' of the 1944 split, NextGen keys Ravi Narayana Reddy (AP History Part 7 p.21). As the Nizam Rashtra Andhra Mahasabha growing out of the Andhra Jana Sangham, the key is Madapati Hanumantha Rao.
Madapati Hanumantha Rao ('Andhra Pitamaha') is credited with starting the Andhra Jana Sangham (1921), which grew into the Nizam Rashtra (State) Andhra Mahasabha; that is how the key reads 'National Andhra Mahasabha'.

options: It was founded in 1930 at Jogipet.

It was established primarily to support the policies of the Nizam Government.
key_text: It was established primarily to support the policies of the Nizam Government.
explanation:
Statement (b) is also inaccurate: Suravaram Pratap Reddy presided over the first (1930) session; Madapati Hanumantha Rao led the earlier Andhra Jana Sangham and presided in 1935 (NextGen Modern India L2 Part 10 p.1). The key keeps (d), the statement meant to be false.
The Mahasabha (Jogipet, 1930) worked for Telugu education and political awareness and opposed the Nizam's autocracy, so (d) is plainly false. Note that the 1930 Jogipet session was presided over by Suravaram Pratap Reddy.
